sources.entry: FineTune - Per-app volume controller with multi-device output and 10-band EQ. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ronitsingh10/FineTune) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: FineTune is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that gives each running app its own volume control, routes audio to different output devices, and provides a 10-band EQ and headphone correction.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you set volume independently for each app, with sliders, mute, and 2x/3x/4x boost presets. Audio can be routed per app to different outputs, or sent to several devices at once, with device priority and auto-restore when a device reconnects. Includes a 10-band EQ with 20 presets, user EQ presets per app, and AutoEQ headphone correction by searching profiles or importing ParametricEQ.txt files. Also offers global hotkeys for app volume up/down/mute, an optional F10–F12 media key and volume HUD override, input device and microphone level control, and DDC control of external monitors. Settings cover menu bar icon styles, light/dark theme, and popup density.
use_cases: control volume of individual apps on mac
send different apps to different speakers or headphones
equalize audio per app or per headphone model
adjust external monitor volume from the mac menu bar
bind keyboard shortcuts for app volume
how_to_run: Download the latest release manually from the GitHub releases page
notable: Per-app volume boost up to 4x combined with per-app EQ and routing
Global hotkeys act on whichever app is currently making sound
Software volume override per device when hardware volume controls don't work
Loudness compensation based on ISO 226:2023 equal-loudness contours
URL schemes for scripting volume and routing
caveats: Needs Screen & System Audio Recording permission on first launch
Only the Homebrew and manual release install paths are described; the README gives no other platforms
